items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: But he had worked with some bands, Vaughn Monroe and that

ctx.x: And your brother took after your father’s instrument.

Yes, right. And Art, well he, during the — when the polio thing happened, he became wheelchair bound, so he had to leave. But he had worked with some bands, Vaughn Monroe and that, and he had utilized, now for the first time, his Fredonia degree. And, sorry, teaching in Delevan High School, which is my alma mater. And from then, he realized at that point that there was a dearth of music for the dance band they called in those days, later they called it the stage band. And he started writing music for his own…
And he thought that there was a market for students to play at that time.
